key_insight: A Quantum Convolutional Neural Network can act as a surrogate model for groundwater heat plume prediction, offering a compact quantum alternative for environmental temperature forecasting.
engineering_relevance: This work shows how quantum models may reduce complex simulation outputs into hardware-friendly targets, which is useful for scalable surrogate modeling in hydrogeology and geothermal system design.
method: Reduced high-dimensional groundwater simulation outputs to compact representative parameters for training.
Built a QCNN with quantum convolution, quantum pooling, and quantum readout layers.
Used Hamiltonian-inspired feature encoding and tested on simulator, noisy, and IBM Kyiv hardware with error mitigation.
evidence_signal: Performance was evaluated with mean squared error on training and testing sets across ideal simulation, noisy simulation, real hardware, and mitigation-enhanced hardware.
watch_item: Current quantum hardware still limits scalability and accuracy, so the QCNN remains less predictive than classical neural networks and depends strongly on noise control and mitigation.
paper_title: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks for Groundwater Heat Plume Prediction: A Surrogate Modeling Approach
